fights.question: Can I stack +2 on +2?
fights.line: Official rules say no. If a +2 hits you, you draw 2 and miss your turn.
fights.rules: A Draw Two makes the next player draw 2 cards and miss their turn, so they never get the chance to pass it on with their own +2.
fights.house: Stacking is the most common house rule. Each player adds a +2 and the last one draws the total. Fine if everyone agrees before the game starts.

fights.question: Do I keep drawing until I can play?
fights.line: You draw one card. If it can be played, you may play it. If not, your turn ends.
fights.rules: When you have nothing to play, you draw a single card. A playable drawn card may go down right away. Otherwise play moves on.
fights.house: Many groups make you keep drawing until you can play. That is a house rule.

fights.question: Can I play +4 when I have the colour?
fights.line: Only when you have no card of the colour on the pile. Matching numbers or symbols are fine.
fights.rules: A Wild Draw Four is only allowed when your hand has no card matching the colour of the discard pile. If you play it anyway, the next player can challenge you.
fights.house: Many groups let you play it any time. That is a house rule.

fights.question: Can I finish on a power card?
fights.line: You can go out on any card. If it is a +2 or +4, the next player still draws.
fights.rules: The round ends when you play your last card, whatever it is. The cards drawn from a final +2 or +4 count when points are added up.
fights.house: Some groups ban going out on an action card. That is not in the Classic rules.

fights.question: Someone forgot to say UNO. Now what?
fights.line: If you catch them before the next player starts their turn, they draw 2 cards.
fights.rules: You must say UNO when you play your second-to-last card. Get caught before the next player begins their turn and you draw 2.
fights.house: Some groups add bigger penalties or let you catch someone any time.

fights.question: Is swapping hands on a 7 a real rule?
fights.line: Not in the Classic rules. Swapping on a 7 or passing hands on a 0 is a house rule.
fights.rules: Classic UNO has no 7 or 0 swap. The only official hand swap is the Wild Shuffle Hands card, which collects and deals out everyone's cards.
fights.house: The 7-0 rule is popular: play a 7 and swap hands with someone, play a 0 and everyone passes hands along. Agree on it before you deal.

fights.question: Can I play a +2 on a +4, or a +4 on a +2?
fights.line: Official rules say no. Whoever is hit draws and misses their turn.
fights.rules: Both cards make the next player draw and lose their turn, so they cannot answer with a draw card of their own.
fights.house: Some groups allow mixing +2 and +4 in a stack. That is a house rule.

fights.question: Can I stack +4 on +4?
fights.line: Official rules say no. If a +4 hits you, you draw 4 and lose your turn.
fights.rules: A Wild Draw Four makes the next player draw 4 and lose their turn, so they cannot play their own +4 back.
fights.house: Some groups stack +4s. That is a house rule.

fights.question: Can I challenge a +4?
fights.line: You can challenge before you draw. They show you their hand.
fights.rules: If they still had a card of the matching colour, they draw the 4 instead of you. If they were allowed to play it, you draw 6.
fights.house: Some groups skip challenges. Then you just draw 4.

fights.question: Can I jump in out of turn with the same card?
fights.line: Not in the Classic rules. You only play on your own turn.
fights.rules: Classic UNO has no jump-in. Each player plays one card on their turn.
fights.house: Jump-in is a popular house rule: anyone holding the exact same card can slap it down out of turn.

fights.question: Can I play two cards of the same number at once?
fights.line: One card per turn in the Classic rules.
fights.rules: On your turn you play a single card that matches by colour, number or symbol.
fights.house: Some groups let you drop several cards of the same number together. That is a house rule.

fights.question: Can I play the card I just drew?
fights.line: Yes, if it can be played, in the same turn.
fights.rules: After drawing because you could not play, or chose not to, you may play the card you drew if it matches. You may not play a different card from your hand.
fights.house: None common.

fights.question: Can I draw even when I have a card I could play?
fights.line: Yes. You may choose to draw one card instead of playing.
fights.rules: If you draw on purpose, you may only play the card you just drew, and only if it matches.
fights.house: None common.

fights.question: Can I play a Wild even when I have other cards I could play?
fights.line: Yes. A plain Wild can go down on any turn.
fights.rules: A Wild can be played on anything, even when you hold other playable cards. The +4 is different: it needs you to have no card of the matching colour.
fights.house: None common.

fights.question: Can I pick the same colour with a Wild?
fights.line: Yes. You can choose any colour, including the one already in play.
fights.rules: When you play a Wild, you pick the colour play continues in, and that can be the current colour.
fights.house: None common.

fights.question: Can I still catch someone for not saying UNO after the next player started?
fights.line: Too late. You have to catch them before the next player begins their turn.
fights.rules: The 2-card penalty only applies if they are caught before the next player starts their turn.
fights.house: Some groups let you catch someone any time.

fights.question: What happens if the first card turned over is an action card?
fights.line: It acts on the first player, except a +4, which goes back in the deck.
fights.rules: Draw Two: the first player draws 2 and misses their turn. Reverse: the dealer starts and play goes right. Skip: the first player is skipped. Wild: the first player picks the colour. Wild Draw Four: put it back and turn over another card.
fights.house: None common.

fights.question: How many points is each card worth?
fights.line: Numbers are face value. Skip, Reverse and +2 are 20. Wild and +4 are 50.
fights.rules: Wild Shuffle Hands and Wild Customizable are 40 each. The round winner scores the cards left in everyone else's hands, and the first to 500 wins.
fights.house: Many groups skip scoring and play single rounds.

fights.question: What if the draw pile runs out?
fights.line: Shuffle the discard pile into a new draw pile and keep playing.
fights.rules: If nobody has gone out when the draw pile is used up, the discard pile is reshuffled to make a new draw pile.
fights.house: None common.

fights.question: What does the Shuffle Hands card do?
fights.line: Everyone's cards are collected, shuffled and dealt back out.
fights.rules: Deal starts with the player to the left of whoever played it, and every card is dealt, so hand sizes can change. It is also a Wild, so that player picks the colour.
fights.house: None common.

fights.question: How many cards does each player start with?
fights.line: 7 cards each.
fights.rules: Everyone draws a card, the highest number deals, and the dealer gives each player 7 cards. The player to the dealer's left goes first.
fights.house: None common.

fights.question: How does the Skip card work?
fights.line: The next player loses their turn.
fights.rules: Play a Skip on a card of the same colour or on another Skip.
fights.house: None common.

fights.question: How does the Reverse card work?
fights.line: Play changes direction.
fights.rules: Play a Reverse on a card of the same colour or on another Reverse.
fights.house: None common.

fights.question: How do you win UNO?
fights.line: Be first to play all your cards each round. First to 500 points wins the game.
fights.rules: The round winner scores the points left in everyone else's hands. Another allowed way: keep a total of the points each player holds, and when someone hits 500, the lowest total wins.
fights.house: Many groups play a single round and the first one out wins.
